title: Authentication System
prompt: Implement registration, login, protected routes, and logout with a vetted authentication approach. Submit a focused JavaScript/Express artifact and explain how you would run and verify it locally. Use synthetic data and test both a normal request and an invalid or failure case.
expected_output: A reviewable implementation for Authentication System with a documented expected response and a local test for one success case and one failure/edge case. CodeLeaf checks required strings only; it does not run submitted Node.js code in the browser.
acceptance_criteria: Address the task: Implement registration, login, protected routes, and logout with a vetted authentication approach.
Use the Express.js 5 syntax and make the required status/response behavior explicit.
Document the local command and show a successful request plus one invalid or dependency-failure request.
Do not include credentials or production data; explain any remaining runtime or security review needed.
hints: Start with the smallest route or middleware that demonstrates the requested concept, then add the validation/error path.
Check the relevant Express 5 guide and the expected status/response shape before changing the example.
Run the server locally and test both a valid request and an invalid/boundary request; capture the result rather than assuming it passed.
grading_method: Server-side case-sensitive required-string smoke check plus human/runtime review. It is not a Node.js sandbox and does not prove that submitted code executes correctly.
retry_policy: Retries permitted after feedback; CodeLeaf records successful completion once. XP is controlled centrally by the backend; this content file defines no reward override.
status_note: Adapted from Section C of ExpressJS.pdf; static grading only checks markers, so manually run and review the implementation before publication.
